<em>Renewable Energy</em>,
<em>Sustainable Development</em>,
<em>Economics of Governance</em> and

<!-- WHAT I'M UP TO -->

<section class="working-section">

  <h2>What I’m up to</h2>


  <details class="project-entry">

    <summary>

      <div class="project-heading">

        <div class="project-title">
          Monetary and Macroprudential Policy in a Polluting Economy
        </div>

        <div class="project-meta">
          with J. Bratsiotis and K. Pathirage
        </div>

      </div>

    </summary>

    <div class="project-description">

      The green transition does not reshape every part of the economy in the
      same way. We attempt to find how differences in environmental exposure,
      investment and finance can shape the macroeconomic effects of climate
      policy.

    </div>

  </details>


  <details class="project-entry">

    <summary>

      <div class="project-heading">

        <div class="project-title">
          Combining Labor Market Reforms and Fiscal Policy in Recessions
        </div>

        <div class="project-meta">
          with Britta Gehrke and Enzo Weber
        </div>

      </div>

    </summary>

    <div class="project-description">

      Reforms rarely happen in a vacuum. We study how the economic environment
      surrounding labour-market reforms can shape their employment consequences,
      with particular attention to the role of fiscal conditions when the
      economy is weak.

    </div>

  </details>


  <details class="project-entry">

    <summary>

      <div class="project-heading">

        <div class="project-title">
          Environmental Debt as a Macroeconomic Vulnerability State
        </div>

        <div class="project-meta">
          with Angeliki Menegaki · Working paper available on request
        </div>

      </div>

    </summary>

    <div class="project-description">

      Ecological pressure is not only an environmental problem. Over time, it
      can become a hidden macroeconomic vulnerability that changes how strongly
      economies react when extreme weather strikes.

    </div>

  </details>


  <details class="project-entry">

    <summary>

      <div class="project-heading">

        <div class="project-title">
          Measuring the Inequality Structure in India
        </div>

        <div class="project-meta">
          with Mridula Debnath
        </div>

      </div>

    </summary>

    <div class="project-description">

      What if places that look equally unequal are not unequal in the same way?
      This project looks beneath standard measures of inequality to study how
      distributional patterns differ across India, and why those differences
      may matter.

    </div>

  </details>


  <details class="project-entry">

    <summary>

      <div class="project-heading">

        <div class="project-title">
          Financing Sustained Mitigation under Unequal Capital Costs:
          Carbon Pricing, Revenue Recycling and External Climate Finance
        </div>

        <div class="project-meta">
          with Angeliki Menegaki · Working paper available on request
        </div>

      </div>

    </summary>

    <div class="project-description">

      Climate ambition is global, but the cost of financing it is not. Unequal
      financial conditions can change the policy mix needed to make sustained
      decarbonisation possible.

    </div>

  </details>


  <details class="project-entry">

    <summary>

      <div class="project-heading">

        <div class="project-title">
          Storage Scarcity and the Inflation Cost of Decarbonisation
        </div>

        <div class="project-meta">
          Working paper version available on request
        </div>

      </div>

    </summary>

    <div class="project-description">

      Clean electricity is not always reliable electricity. Storage scarcity
      can turn the energy transition into a macroeconomic problem, changing how
      shocks pass through to prices, inflation, and output.

    </div>

  </details>

</section>
